messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P2 - Multiple customer egress errors observed in us-west-2 (AZ3). Alert: NAT Gateway healthcheck failing 5xx and conntrack saturation on some nodes. https://alerts.redwood.example/alerts/9876 :rotating_light:
Maya (infra): seeing spike in 502/504s to external APIs from tasks in private-subnet-az3. Dashboards show NAT gateway with unhealthy target ENI.
Tom H: confirming. I can ssh to a bastion and curl outgoing URL from a sample task?
Maya (infra): yeah try from pod on subnet-az3: nsenter into container and run `curl -v https://api.external-service.com/health`
Tom H: curl times out with TLS handshake failure, but ping resolves.
Natalie S: packet captures show SYN out but no SYN-ACK back for some flows. Might be SNAT mapping lost (conntrack).
Leo R: looking at NAT metrics in console — TX/RX dropped increased at 12:27 UTC and health check failing for the primary ENI. AWS shows ENI detached then reattached briefly.
Maya (infra): this smells like ephemeral maintenance on NAT gateway or a bad route table referencing a stale ENI. Can someone check route table for private-subnet-az3?
Tom H: route table shows default route -> nat-xxxx (in AZ3), looks correct.
Natalie S: checking VPC flow logs for refused connections. I see `REJECT` from AZ3 NAT to internet gw on port 443 starting 12:26.
Maya (infra): rolling mitigation options: 1) create new NAT gateway in AZ3 and swap route 2) temporarily natting via NAT instance in AZ2 and update route priority 3) force_failover on Dedicated NAT (if supported).
CS Ops - Priya: customers on enterprise plans are seeing failures in webhook deliveries. Any ETA?
Maya (infra): estimating 30-45m if we build new NAT and swap. Trying faster: create NAT instance (t3.small) and update route table as short-term.
Tom H: launching NAT instance now. Terraform will take ~2m. Sharing commands:```bash
# launch instance and enable ip_forwarding
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0abcd1234 --subnet-id subnet-az3-private --instance-type t3.small --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=temp-nat-az3}]'
# enable ip forwarding and configure iptables SNAT
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```
Leo R: created instance, IP 10.0.123.45. Adding security group to allow outbound 0.0.0.0/0 and inbound from private subnets on ephemeral ports.
Maya (infra): applying route table change to point 0.0.0.0/0 to instance eni-attach-zzz (temporary). Will apply to rtb-az3-private.
oncall-bot: oncall handoff requested: @Maya (infra) is primary until 13:30 UTC then @Tom H will take over.
Maya (infra): route update applied. Please validate egress from a couple of pods.
Tom H: tested curl from two pods in az3 -> success 200, latency ~80ms. Looks good.
Natalie S: monitoring for conntrack drain. `conntrack -S` on NAT instance shows <1K entries initially. Previous NAT had ~200k entries. That likely caused existing NAT to struggle.
CS Ops - Priya: notifying impacted customers with short blurb: "We're seeing transient outbound connectivity issues from services in us-west-2 AZ3; mitigation in progress; we'll update within 30m."
Maya (infra): initial customer impact: ~12% of active tasks were pinned to az3; estimate 9% of API call failures across production tenants.
Leo R: filing incident ticket with preliminary severity P2 and customers impacted list.
Tom H: keeping temp NAT instance while we investigate root cause and request AWS support for ENI health. Opening support case SR-55099.
incident-bot: AWS support case created SR-55099 by Maya (infra). Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=SR-55099
Natalie S: quick postmortem pointers being collected: conntrack growth + NAT ENI flapping. Need to check if policy on connection timeout changed or if upstream API is using long-lived connections.
Maya (infra): agreed. Action items: 1) keep temp NAT for 2h and drain flows 2) collect conntrack logs from original NAT 3) increase NAT capacity or split subnets across AZs 4) add alert for conntrack saturation and ENI detach.
Tom H: handing off monitoring to @Tom H for the next 2 hours. Leaving a note in oncall channel.
oncall-bot: handoff complete: @Tom H is now oncall for this incident.
CS Ops - Priya: will coordinate outbound customer comms and update status page.
Maya (infra): marking in incident tracker: root_cause_hypothesis="ENI flapping on managed NAT + conntrack exhaustion causing SNAT failures".
Natalie S: also capture a snippet of iptables counters from affected tasks and NAT:```bash
# on nat
sudo iptables -t nat -nvL
# conntrack dump
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
```
Leo R: follow-ups added to tracker: terraform modules to support quick replacement, playbook runbook for nat-instance fallback, and metric for conntrack usage.
Maya (infra): moving thread to incident postmortem once stabilized. Thanks all for fast response. :clap:
Tom H: leaving note: temp NAT will be decommissioned after 2h and route table restored to managed NAT if AWS completes ENI fix.
CS Ops - Priya: updating customers: "Mitigation in place; services routing via temporary NAT instance. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause and timeline."
incident-bot: Ticket updated: status=mitigated_by_route_swap, mitigated_at=1799998855
Maya (infra): incident status -> mitigated, monitoring for regressions. Postmortem owner: Natalie S.
